gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-persi: Noto Sans Old Persian reads tall and open, with room around every curve. Edo SZ is the oddity above it, a display face drawn like outlines in a single width, and that tension is the pair's real hook.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdi: Noto Sans Old Sogdian reads crisp and friendly, its tall lowercase nearly touching cap height and its wide mouths staying sharp when small. Edo SZ holds a constant line around every curve, while the plain sans does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Compass-pencil lines, cast-iron stature. Noto Sans Old Turkic follows with chunky, tall lowercase and open-mouthed curves, so the pair's strongest quality is how sturdy it looks next to Edo SZ's single steady stroke.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Edo SZ draws everything with one plain, unshaded line that never swells. That is its best trick, while Noto Sans Oriya does its own work with generous curve gaps and small letters nearly as tall as the capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-osage: Wire-bright letters with round rims. Edo SZ earns its keep big and short, and Noto Sans Osage fills the line beneath with inflated bowls and sweeping curves that stay open.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Edo SZ looks thin yet has no thinner parts anywhere. It is built for display, while Noto Sans Osmanya handles the text with easy-turning s shapes and a lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hm: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong reads high and crisp, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle. Edo SZ sits over it with strokes that look cut from wire, so a delicate heading meets a lofty, open body.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Wire-thin lines, no swelling anywhere. Edo SZ is made for display, while Noto Sans Palmyrene is the plain sans for text, with curves that stop short and compressed ascenders.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-h: Edo SZ keeps a steady line with no pressure variation at all. And if it were shrunk down, that wiry quality would fade, whereas Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau stays open and breathing at any small size.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Noto Sans PhagsPa reads open and approachable, with c openings you can see through and a gentle step up to capitals. And Edo SZ, drawn like a ballpoint pen line, adds a cast-iron, historical mood above it.
